neighbours.label: 'brand name(s)' or 'trade name(s)' in a parenthesis right after a drug's generic name (a sub-trigger of a broad pole)
fire: Atorvastatin (brand names: Lipitor, Torvast) lowers cholesterol in the blood.
Ibuprofen (brand names Advil and Motrin) relieves mild pain.
The sedative diazepam (trade names: Valium, Diastat) is widely prescribed.
Patients take sertraline (brand name: Zoloft) once each morning.
Omeprazole (trade names Prilosec, Losec) reduces stomach acid.
The antibiotic amoxicillin (brand names include Amoxil) treats ear infections.
Insulin glargine (brand name Lantus) is injected once a day.
Fluoxetine (trade name Prozac) was approved for use in 1987.
quiet: Atorvastatin (a common statin drug) lowers cholesterol in the blood.
Ibuprofen (often taken with food) relieves mild pain.
The sedative diazepam (first sold in 1963) is widely prescribed.
Patients take sertraline (usually as a tablet) once each morning.
Omeprazole (sold over the counter) reduces stomach acid.
The antibiotic amoxicillin (also given to children) treats ear infections.
Insulin glargine (a long-acting form) is injected once a day.
Fluoxetine (an older antidepressant) was approved for use in 1987.

short: parenthetical brand or trade name after a drug
notes: Card: broad (3.2% of tokens at 0.1 of max), peaks on function words (that, with, to, as, any) plus one 'brand' in a Warfarin definition. Probe: 'brand' 0.80 or 0.25, 'names' 0.47, 'famous brand' 0.03; function words after their verb reach only 0.11-0.31, too weak to test. So this is only a sub-trigger; expect it to be partial at best.
